script.base: Books have LAC leading a moderate dome game at the 25.0-18.5 implied split, not a shootout. Herbert can throw (week 1: McConkey 7/82/97 air, Njoku 5/58) while Hampton, the lead back at 12 of 21 team rushes, adds late carries if the -6.5 lead holds. LV, with Cousins the week-1 QB (2 rushes), trails and cannot turn Jeanty's 23-carry, 102-yard script into another 100-yard day against a front that allowed 3.84 YPC.
script.flip1: LV stays within one score into the fourth. Jeanty keeps 20-plus carries and one 10-plus run (LAC already allowed 3) can clear 102.5, Hampton never gets clock-kill volume and stays near his 12-carry, 43-yard week, and LV does not have to abandon the run.
script.flip2: LAC is up 17-plus early. Jeanty's carries die (helps the under) but Herbert/McConkey/Njoku sit late, Hampton's extra carries come with Pipkins out so efficiency can pin him near 43.5, and LV's pass volume (Mayer 7 targets, Nailor 64 air yards) spikes in garbage time.

injury_fallout: Pre-game nflverse report, inactives not locked: LV TE Brock Bowers Doubtful (knee) but he is absent from the week-1 target list, so Mayer's 7/32/28 already looks like the TE1 share and is not a fresh spike. LV CB Darien Porter Out (foot) weakens the secondary LAC throws at. LV QB Aidan O'Connell Questionable (personal); Cousins is the week-1 rusher, so a start swap is unpriced. LAC T Trey Pipkins Out (knee): rushing efficiency down, pressure and quick throws up, which caps Hampton's YPC and nudges TE/RB catches. LAC S Elijah Molden Out (hamstring) helps deep shots (Nailor 64 air, Tucker 50 air), not the run. LAC WR Ladd McConkey Questionable (rib) and CB Deane Leonard Questionable (abdomen) are game-time; if McConkey is limited, Johnston (6/17), Harris (6/20), Njoku (5/58) and Gadsden (2/32) absorb targets. Hampton's overlap is volume against a 4.11 YPC front, not an explosive-run funnel (only 2 runs of 10+).

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost. LAC's 3.84 YPC was one game, the +6.5 never forced a full abandon, and Jeanty — 23 carries and 6 targets, the whole LV offense — got another 21-plus carries plus one of the 10-plus runs that front already allows and cleared 102.5. Hampton never got the script bump: Pipkins wrecked the edge, LV's 4.11 YPC did not matter because LAC fell behind, Herbert kept designed runs, and Hampton finished near 11 carries and under 43.5. These lines are last week's stats, not a mispriced book, so a one-game story was the whole edge.
